description: Fifth eval set (v5) for the knowledge VS Code extension: 14 blast-radius engineering tasks that are provably cross-repository (every case requires >=3 repos) AND grep-resistant. Uses ONLY repositories present on disk (react, redux, redux-toolkit, react-redux, reselect, redux-thunk, jotai, zustand, db, xyflow, query, table); MiMo-Code is on disk but excluded (not reactive-ecosystem). v5 = the 10 v4 cases re-verified against current disk (all pinned commits unchanged) with three classes of fixes — (1) every redux-toolkit path corrected to the real monorepo location packages/toolkit/src/... (all 11 v4 RTK paths were broken on disk), (2) stale-by-move files replaced (db collection notification loop moved to collection/changes.ts; jotai store.ts is now a facade over internals.ts), (3) genuinely-required files from the query/table repos (cloned 2026-07-30, after v4 authoring) added to the expected sets — plus 4 NEW cases centered on query and table coupling. Each item's `expected` lists the minimum set of repos/files a correct change must touch. Every listed file path was re-verified against the on-disk checkout at the pinned commits in `repoVersions`. knowledgeId = md5("owner/repo").
repoVersionsNote: branch and commit reflect the on-disk checkout at authoring time (verified via git). NOTE: react has moved since v3 (was 172742b, now f598ec1); all react paths in this file were re-verified at the new commit. [2026-08-02] Six repos re-pinned to the indexing layer's commits (react 3a717e42, redux-toolkit b1c51301, query 9d24c455, react-redux ad5d1e08, reselect 8d87c27b, redux 3aa561f9); all 14 cases' expected paths, key import couplings, and the query line-number citations (:132, :305) re-verified unchanged at the new commits.
grepResistanceNote: Unlike v2/v3, the questions deliberately avoid the identifiers that appear in the target files (no 'useSyncExternalStore', 'Dispatch', 'Middleware', 'createContext', '__REDUX_DEVTOOLS_EXTENSION__', 'weakMapMemoize', 'thenable' in the question text). Grepping the question's own nouns ('observe a data source', 'interception pipeline', 'time-travel debugging', 'state-transition event') returns zero relevant hits, or — for generic words like 'snapshot'/'subscribe'/'listener' — thousands of hits spread across ~10 repos with no ranking. Retrieval therefore has to be structural or semantic, not lexical: (1) resolve each repo's public surface from package.json exports -> entry index files; (2) walk the cross-repo import graph for edges that import the coupled package ('zustand/traditional' inside xyflow, 'redux-thunk' inside redux-toolkit, 'use-sync-external-store/shim' inside zustand/react-redux); (3) map the question's behavioral vocabulary onto API concepts (a knowledge-graph / embedding index does this in one hop; an agent without one must read entry points and follow re-export chains).
benchmarkNote: Cost/time model for a grep-free agentic retrieval, ASSUMING NO PROMPT CACHING (no cache read or write): every API request re-bills the FULL accumulated context (system prompt + tool schemas ~12,000 tok + question ~400 tok + all tool results so far) at the normal input rate. contentTokens = measured on-disk bytes/4 of everything the agent must pull in (per-repo directory listing + package.json + entry/index hop + the full expected files). turns = agent tool-call turns modeled as repos+3 (list folder; batch-read package.jsons+entries; follow import edges; read targets; final answer). billedInputTokens = turns*(system+question) + contentTokens*turns/2 (content accumulates linearly across turns and is re-sent every subsequent request). outputTokens = ~100/intermediate turn (tool calls) + ~300 final answer. costUsd = billedInput/1e6*5.00 + output/1e6*25.00 (Opus 4.8: $5 in / $25 out per Mtok). retrievalTimeSeconds = MEASURED wall-clock of the local file reads only; estimatedAgentSeconds = turns*3.5s (API round-trip + generation) + 2s, the realistic end-to-end latency. Caveats: hidden reasoning tokens are not billed here, and an agent that wanders into wrong candidate files before the right ones can easily 2-3x contentTokens — treat these as the FLOOR for grep-free retrieval. Costs are reported for BOTH claude-opus-4-8 ($5/$25 per Mtok) and claude-fable-5 ($10/$50 per Mtok — note: there is no 'Opus 5'; Fable 5 is the Claude 5 family flagship). Totals live in the `totals` block.

cases.question: React tightens the rules for how a component may observe a data source that lives outside the renderer: the value read during render must now be referentially stable between render and commit, and the cleanup timing of the observation changes under concurrent re-renders. Every library in this folder that bridges its own state container into React components has such a bridge layer. Which files in which repositories implement that bridge and must change?
cases.why_cross_repo: The contract lives in react (`packages/react/src/ReactHooks.js` for the built-in hook, `packages/use-sync-external-store/src/useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector.js` for the shim two libraries consume). zustand's React binding (`src/react.ts`) calls `React.useSyncExternalStore` directly; react-redux's `useSelector` goes through the shim via its typing file (`src/hooks/useSelector.ts`, `src/utils/useSyncExternalStore.ts`); TanStack DB's `useLiveQuery` (`packages/react-db/src/useLiveQuery.ts`) builds a subscribe/getSnapshot pair from a collection. One react contract change hits three independent bridge layers that never import each other. v5 additions: zustand's second bridge useStoreWithEqualityFn (src/traditional.ts:36), react-redux's connect HOC (src/components/connect.tsx:742 calls useSyncExternalStore), and TanStack Query's five uSES bridges (react-query useBaseQuery.ts:107, useQueries.ts:269, useMutation.ts:42, useIsFetching.ts:15, useMutationState.ts:57). table does NOT qualify (useReactTable binds via plain useState); jotai uses useReducer; preact-query targets Preact, not React. [v5 revision: re-verified against current disk with query/table repos present; expected set updated accordingly.]
cases.grep_resistance: The question never says 'useSyncExternalStore', 'getSnapshot' or 'subscribe'. Grepping 'observe'/'data source'/'bridge' finds nothing relevant; grepping 'snapshot' returns hundreds of unranked hits across react, db, and zustand. The reliable route is the import graph: find who imports 'use-sync-external-store/shim' or calls the React 18 store hook.

Which wrapper components and injection points across the folder are built on this mechanism and must be revisited?
cases.why_cross_repo: The mechanism is react's context (`packages/react/src/ReactContext.js`). Three libraries independently build store-injection wrappers on it: react-redux (`src/components/Context.ts` + `src/components/Provider.tsx`), jotai (`src/react/Provider.ts`), and xyflow, whose `ReactFlowProvider` creates a zustand store and injects it via a React context (`packages/react/src/contexts/StoreContext.ts`, `packages/react/src/components/ReactFlowProvider/index.tsx`). None of the three import each other; only the react contract couples them. v5 addition: TanStack Query's QueryClientProvider (packages/react-query/src/QueryClientProvider.tsx:6-41 — createContext<QueryClient>, useQueryClient nearest-ancestor lookup, Provider component consumed by every hook). zustand has no built-in context; table is headless (no createContext); db's react package exposes no store-injection context (verified). cases.question: The definition of what counts as a legitimate state-transition event — a tagged plain object, plus the runtime guards that decide 'is this a plain object?' and 'is this a valid event?' — becomes stricter (e.g. prototype-chain rules change). Which repos re-export those guards, depend on them for invariant checking, or hand-roll a parallel implementation of the same event model that must stay consistent?
cases.why_cross_repo: The event model and guards live in redux (`src/types/actions.ts`, `src/utils/isAction.ts`, `src/utils/isPlainObject.ts`). redux-toolkit re-exports the guards through its import boundary (`src/reduxImports.ts`) and leans on plain-object detection in `src/serializableStateInvariantMiddleware.ts`. zustand's redux middleware (`src/middleware/redux.ts`) hand-implements the same tagged-object event model without importing redux, so a stricter contract must be mirrored there to keep the two reducer models consistent — three repos, one semantic contract. v5 addition: react-redux hand-rolls the identical prototype-chain plain-object guard (src/utils/isPlainObject.ts, consumed by verifyPlainObject.ts) — a fork that must stay consistent when the prototype rules tighten. TanStack Query's isPlainObject (query-core utils) uses a different algorithm for cache-data structural sharing, not the event model — excluded; table has no such guard. RTK paths corrected to packages/toolkit/src/. [v5 revision: re-verified against current disk with query/table repos present; expected set updated accordingly.]

Only concept-level retrieval (or prior knowledge that zustand ships a redux-style middleware) surfaces the third repo.

TanStack DB throws a loading promise from its Suspense hook (`packages/react-db/src/useLiveSuspenseQuery.ts`). One react protocol change hits two async feeders that share no code. v5 additions (query repo, cloned after v4 authoring): TanStack Query is the most explicit React-thenable shim in the folder — packages/query-core/src/thenable.ts authors Thenable types 'matching React's promise shape' and pendingThenable()/tryResolveSync() fabricate stamped pending values; queryObserver.ts maintains #currentThenable and exposes it as result.promise (:591); react-query useBaseQuery.ts throws fetchOptimistic() into render (:132); useQueries.ts throws a raw unstamped Promise.all(suspensePromises) (:305). cases.question: Across these libraries there's a recurring pattern: when the user's browser tab comes back to the foreground after being hidden, or when the device's network link is restored after dropping, any work that was deferred, paused, or has gone stale is automatically re-attempted or re-validated. Each library hand-wires the raw browser signals — the page-became-visible-again notification and the connectivity-came-back notification — into its own 'now is a good time to re-run' trigger, and each also decides whether an in-flight or held operation may resume based on whether the page is currently attended-to and the machine is currently reachable. Suppose we change that contract so a resume/revalidate trigger must carry a reason token describing which of the two conditions fired (regained attention vs. regained connectivity), and so that being in the foreground no longer gates resumption on its own. Find every file that subscribes to those browser conditions or gates resumption on them and would have to change.
cases.why_cross_repo: TanStack Query wires 'page visible again' in packages/query-core/src/focusManager.ts (visibilitychange listener :17-36, setEventListener/onFocus :47-67) and 'network back' in packages/query-core/src/onlineManager.ts (online/offline listeners :15-27, setEventListener/setOnline :48-60); packages/query-core/src/retryer.ts gates continuation on both (canContinue uses focusManager.isFocused() && onlineManager.isOnline() :105-106, pause/resume :125,196-224). RTK Query independently hand-wires the same two conditions in packages/toolkit/src/query/core/setupListeners.ts (visibilitychange/focus/online/offline handlers :80-116 dispatching onFocus/onOnline actions :15-33). TanStack DB's offline outbox re-implements detection in packages/offline-transactions/src/connectivity/OnlineDetector.ts (WebOnlineDetector listens to online + visibilitychange :25-26, subscribe :66) and consumes it in packages/offline-transactions/src/OfflineExecutor.ts (onlineDetector.subscribe drains the outbox :225, unsubscribe :603-605). A reason-token/gating change forces edits in all three repos' subscription and gate sites.

It is phrased behaviorally ('tab comes back to the foreground', 'network link is restored', 'now is a good time to re-run', 'gates resumption', 'reason token'), so keyword grep over the question's nouns cannot surface the coupled files.

cases.question: Three of these libraries each independently roll their own policy for spacing out repeated attempts at an operation that keeps failing: the pause before the next try grows geometrically with the count of consecutive failures (roughly doubling each round), is clamped to a maximum ceiling so it never runs away, and after a bounded number of attempts the operation stops retrying and surfaces the failure. Some variants also fuzz the wait with a random component to avoid synchronized retries. Suppose we change this contract so the wait must be derived from wall-clock time elapsed since the first failure rather than from the attempt count, and so the ceiling becomes mandatory rather than optional. Find every self-contained implementation of the failed-attempt spacing/give-up policy that would have to be rewritten.
cases.why_cross_repo: TanStack Query computes the geometric-with-cap delay in packages/query-core/src/retryer.ts (defaultRetryDelay = Math.min(1000 * 2 ** failureCount, 30000) :49-50; shouldRetry/failureCount++ give-up logic :169-186). RTK Query hand-rolls its own copy in packages/toolkit/src/query/retry.ts (defaultBackoff :26-33 with Math.min(attempt, maxRetries) and jittered doubling ~~((Math.random()+0.4)*(300<<attempts))). TanStack DB's offline outbox has a third implementation split across packages/offline-transactions/src/retry/BackoffCalculator.ts (Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, retryCount), 60000) + jitter :9-11) and packages/offline-transactions/src/retry/RetryPolicy.ts (calculateDelay :14-15, shouldRetry enforcing maxRetries :18-23). Same behavioral contract written three times; deriving the wait from elapsed time instead of attempt count forces edits in each repo's delay-and-give-up site.

Suppose we change the shape of that ordered-input gate — say the element-wise reference test becomes a supplied comparator, or the instrumentation hook's signature changes. Which files implement this list-of-inputs recompute barrier and its timing/recount hook, and would all need to move together?

cases.question: A convention shows up in all of these libraries: a writable piece of state whose write API accepts two interchangeable shapes — either a bare replacement value, or a callback that is handed the current value and returns the next one. At the write site each library does a runtime typeof-function fork: if it's a function it invokes it against the previous snapshot to derive the new value, otherwise it takes the argument as-is. Critically, the owner of that state may live outside the component that renders it — one library lets you hand ownership of the whole state bag to an external listener while still defaulting to internally-held state, and its React binding forwards the very same value-or-callback argument straight through into the framework's own setter so a caller can control just a subset. Another applies the same fork when you write into a keyed cache entry, running your callback against the previously-cached datum. If we tightened or widened the accepted shapes of this writer (e.g. added an async producer form, or passed a second argument to the callback), which files defining or applying this value-or-previous-callback convention would have to change in lockstep?

Widening the writer's accepted shapes forces coordinated edits across table, query, zustand and xyflow.
